title: Inverting functions in the Drury–Arveson space for dimension 5
statement: Let $H^2_5$ be the Drury–Arveson space of analytic functions on the unit ball $B_5\subset\mathbb{C}^5$ such that, for $f(z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{N}^5}a_nz^n$, $\|f\|_{H^2_5}^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{N}^5}|a_n|^2\frac{n!}{|n|!}<\infty$, where $|n|=n_1+\cdots+n_5$ and $n!=n_1!\cdots n_5!$. If $f\in H^2_5$ and $|f(z)|\ge 1$ for every $z\in B_5$, must $1/f\in H^2_5$?
completeness_reason: Norm, ball and inverse-membership assertion explicitly defined.
literal_quantifiers: Every analytic f with finite stated norm and pointwise modulus at least one.
technical_assessment: Inverse-closedness for this Hilbert function space needs a global coefficient estimate; zero-free analyticity alone does not bound this norm. No short full-scope route identified.

title: Boundary terms for vanishing-viscosity stochastic perturbations
statement: The bulk part $J^0$ of the dynamic functional ([17]) governs large deviations for a vanishing-viscosity stochastic perturbation of equation (2). Can one add boundary conditions to this stochastic equation and obtain the boundary terms for the dynamic large deviations?
completeness_reason: Equation (2), functional [17] and stochastic perturbation are absent.
literal_quantifiers: Boundary-condition existence for an unspecified stochastic equation.
technical_assessment: Cannot choose boundary law or rate functional without the missing model; retain literal rather than replace.

title: Monotonicity of the diffusion coefficient in the particle density
statement: For every fixed \b3>0, the diffusion coefficient $D_\b3(\d70)$ is decreasing as a function of the density $\d70$ on $[0,1]$.
completeness_reason: D and the particle dynamics are undefined; escaped parameter symbols are corrupted.
literal_quantifiers: Every positive parameter, all densities in [0,1], monotone coefficient.
technical_assessment: An exclusion-process variational formula and its density dependence would be needed; arbitrary diffusion coefficients need not be monotone.

title: Homotopy groups of rapidly decreasing mapping groups
statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer and let $H$ be a Lie group modelled on a locally convex space. For every $k=1,2,\ldots$, the homotopy groups satisfy

$$\pi_k\bigl(S(\mathbb{R}^m,H)\bigr)=\pi_{k+m}(H).$$
completeness_reason: Rapid-decay mapping space S and its topology are not defined.
literal_quantifiers: All locally convex Lie groups H, all positive m,k.
technical_assessment: Compactification suggests an iterated-loop comparison, but smooth rapid decay and parameter-dependent approximation for arbitrary locally convex models are real obligations.

title: Ext-groups for affine Hecke algebras and their Schwartz completions
statement:
Let $H$ be an affine Hecke algebra with positive parameters, let $\[200m\pi,\[0m\pi'$ be finite-dimensional tempered $H$-modules, and let $S$ be the Schwartz completion of $H$. Then, for every $i\in\mathbb{Z}$, there is an isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_{H}(\pi,\pi')\simeq \operatorname{Ext}^{i}_{S}(\pi,\pi').
$$
Consequently, $EP_H(\pi,\pi')=EP_S(\pi,\pi')$.
completeness_reason: Exact category of S-modules and Ext, including negative degrees, is unspecified; typesetting escapes are damaged.
literal_quantifiers: All positive-parameter affine Hecke algebras, tempered finite-dimensional pairs, every integer i.
technical_assessment: An isocohomological completion theorem would be needed; no proof or category bridge established. Possible existing theorem is only an unverified lead.

title: Vanishing of the simplicial volume of the moduli space of closed Riemann surfaces
statement: For every integer $g\ge 1$, the simplicial volume of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_g$ is equal to $0$.
completeness_reason: Noncompact orbifold moduli space needs ordinary versus locally finite simplicial-volume convention.
literal_quantifiers: Every genus g at least one.
technical_assessment: Ordinary and locally finite fundamental-class arguments differ; a noncompactness shortcut would change the intended question.

title: Non-varying sum of Lyapunov exponents in hyperelliptic strata
statement: For all hyperelliptic strata, the sum of Lyapunov exponents is non-varying.
completeness_reason: Non-varying does not state over which invariant measures or curves, or which Lyapunov cocycle.
literal_quantifiers: All hyperelliptic strata, an unspecified variation family.
technical_assessment: Hyperelliptic formulas are a plausible public-result lead; without measure and cocycle scope no full bridge is claimed.

title: Nielsen realization problem for finite quasiconformal mapping class subgroups
statement: Let $R$ be a Riemann surface admitting a hyperbolic structure, let $\operatorname{MCG}(R)$ be its quasiconformal mapping class group, and let $q:\operatorname{QC}(R)\to\operatorname{MCG}(R)$ be the natural surjection. For every finite subgroup $\Gamma\leq\operatorname{MCG}(R)$, there exists a homomorphism $E:\Gamma\to\operatorname{QC}(R)$ such that $q\circ E=\operatorname{id}_{\Gamma}$.
completeness_reason: Surface, quasiconformal group, quotient and splitting requirement are specified.
literal_quantifiers: Every hyperbolic-type Riemann surface and every finite subgroup of its quasiconformal mapping class group.
technical_assessment: Finite-type Nielsen realization cannot simply be extended to all surfaces in the literal domain; uniform quasiconformal realization is the obstruction.

title: Andreadakis conjecture for the automorphism group of a free group
statement:
Let $F_n$ be a free group of rank $n\ge 2$, let $IA_n=A'_n(1)$ be its IA-automorphism group, let $A'_n(1),A'_n(2),\ldots$ be the lower central series of $IA_n$, and let $A_n(1),A_n(2),\ldots$ be the Johnson filtration of $\operatorname{Aut}F_n$. The Andreadakis conjecture asks whether
\[
A'_n(k)=A_n(k)
\]
for every $k\ge 1$ (for each $n\ge 2$).
completeness_reason: Two filtrations and both integer ranges are specified using standard group notions.
literal_quantifiers: Every n at least two and k at least one.
technical_assessment: Low-degree computations cannot prove equality of infinite filtrations. Known-counterexample recollection is an unverified prior lead, not a body clearance or novelty claim.

title: Strict positivity for the fourth-order quantum diffusion equation
statement:
For the fourth-order quantum diffusion equation

$$
\partial_t n+\operatorname{div}\!\left(n\nabla\left(\frac{\Delta\sqrt n}{\sqrt n}\right)\right)=0,
\qquad n(\cdot,0)=n_0\ge 0\ \text{in }\mathbb T^d,
$$

is the solution strictly positive for every $t>0$, even if the nonnegative initial datum vanishes at some point?
completeness_reason: Solution class, dimension bounds and nonzero-mass hypothesis are absent at the singular quotient sqrt(n).
literal_quantifiers: Every positive time for unspecified solutions and nonnegative initial data on a torus.
technical_assessment: Zero datum and weak-solution interpretation require source repair; no positivity result or credit from that endpoint correction.

title: Simonovits–Sidorenko conjecture
statement: For every bipartite graph $F$, the functional $t(F,W)-t(K_2,W)^{|E(F)|}$ is minimized by constant functions $W$, where $W$ ranges over graphons.
completeness_reason: Finite bipartite graphs, graphons and standard homomorphism densities specify a precise inequality.
literal_quantifiers: Every bipartite F and graphon W; minimum zero at constants.
technical_assessment: Tree and even-cycle inequalities do not cover arbitrary bipartite F. No bounded full-family mechanism identified.

title: Local out-neighbour chromatic number versus global tournament chromatic number
statement: For all $k \ge 0$ there exists $c$ such that, if $G$ is a tournament in which the set of out-neighbours of each vertex has chromatic number at most $k$, then $\chi(G) \le c$.
completeness_reason: Tournament chromatic number can mean acyclic coloring or underlying undirected coloring.
literal_quantifiers: For every k there is c uniform over all tournaments with locally bounded out-neighborhood color number.
technical_assessment: Underlying-graph interpretation is trivial by degree bound, whereas intended directed coloring needs a different local-to-global theorem. No credit for that convention shortcut.

title: Vertex-disjoint directed paths in semicomplete digraphs
statement: For every fixed integer $k$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a semicomplete digraph $G$, vertices $s_1,t_1,\ldots,s_k,t_k$ of $G$, and integers $x_1,\ldots,x_k\ge 0$, decides whether there exist pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths $P_1,\ldots,P_k$ in $G$ such that, for each $1\le i\le k$, $P_i$ is a path from $s_i$ to $t_i$ having at most $x_i$ vertices.
completeness_reason: Finite input, fixed parameter, disjointness and path length caps are explicit.
literal_quantifiers: Each fixed nonnegative path count k; all semicomplete inputs and all per-path budgets.
technical_assessment: Enumerating paths is exponential; unbounded-length linkage algorithms do not automatically handle individual budgets. No justified polynomial dynamic program supplied.

title: Forcing conjecture for bipartite graphs with two complete vertices
statement: The forcing conjecture holds for every bipartite graph $H$ which has two vertices in one part complete to the other part, which has at least two vertices.
completeness_reason: The forcing conjecture itself is not stated.
literal_quantifiers: All bipartite H with two vertices universal to the opposite part of size at least two.
technical_assessment: Need exact density equality and quasirandomness conclusion before a Cauchy-Schwarz equality-case bridge; method similarity alone is insufficient.

title: Right-convergence of sparse Erdős–Rényi graphs
statement:
For every fixed $c>0$, does the sequence of sparse Erdős–Rényi graphs $G(n,c/n)$ right-converge with high probability; that is, for every finite weighted graph $H$ with a symmetric nonnegative weight matrix $w$, does
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log h\bigl(G(n,c/n),H\bigr)
\]
exist with high probability, where $h(G,H)$ is the weighted homomorphism sum defined in the report?
completeness_reason: Weighted homomorphism sum h is explicitly deferred to the report.
literal_quantifiers: Every c positive and every nonnegative weighted target; normalized log limit in probability-like wording.
technical_assessment: Zero weights can force zero partition functions; normalization and meaning of high-probability existence matter. No free-energy interpolation proof attempted.

title: Euclidean Ramsey conjecture for spherical finite configurations
statement: For every finite point set $K$ that can be embedded in a sphere and every positive integer $r$, does there exist an integer $d_0(K,r)$ such that, for every integer $d\ge d_0(K,r)$, every $r$-coloring of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a monochromatic isometric copy of $K$?
completeness_reason: Finite spherical configuration, colors, dimensions and isometric copies are specified.
literal_quantifiers: Every spherical finite K, every positive r, eventually every d and every coloring.
technical_assessment: Finite enumerations of colorings cannot settle arbitrary dimension or continuous Euclidean colorings; no full route.

title: Weak selections and weak orderability
statement: Is every topological space which admits a weak selection weakly orderable? Here a weak selection on a topological space $X$ is a continuous function $\[${X}^{2}$\]$ to $X$ such that $\[\varphi(x,y)=\varphi(y,x)\in\{x,y\}\]$ for every $x,y\in X$, and $X$ is weakly orderable if it admits a weaker linearly ordered topology.
completeness_reason: Malformed displayed domain and unordered-pair versus X squared topology leave weak selection continuity ambiguous.
literal_quantifiers: Every topological space admitting a continuous weak selection.
technical_assessment: Diagonal, hyperspace and separation assumptions must be recovered before an order-topology construction; no literal repair promoted.

title: Classification under weaker assumptions than Maharam’s theorem
statement: Can a characterization analogous to Maharam’s classification be obtained for pairs $(B,\mu)$ in which $B$ is an arbitrary Boolean algebra, not necessarily $\sigma$-complete, and $\mu$ is a strictly positive finitely additive measure on $B$, normalized so that $\mu(1_B)=1$?
completeness_reason: Analogous characterization has no stated equivalence or classification invariant.
literal_quantifiers: All Boolean algebras with strictly positive normalized finitely additive measure.
technical_assessment: Maharam-type completion alone may forget the original algebra; desired classification standard is missing.

title: Mazur’s rotation problem
statement: Any separable Banach space $X$ whose norm is transitive—that is, for every two points $x,y$ on the unit sphere of $X$, there exists a surjective linear isometry $T:X\to X$ such that $Tx=y$—is isometric to $\ell_2$.
completeness_reason: Infinite dimensionality and real/complex scalar convention are absent; literal ell2 excludes finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
literal_quantifiers: All separable transitive-norm Banach spaces.
technical_assessment: Finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces contradict the literal endpoint but only correct its intended domain; no substantive outcome or credit.

title: Bárány–Larman conjecture for the alternative colored Tverberg function
statement:
Let $t(d,r)$ be the function defined in the report’s alternative colored Tverberg problem. The Bárány–Larman conjecture asserts that
\[
t(d,r)=r\qquad\text{for all integers }d\ge 1\text{ and }r\ge 2.
\]
completeness_reason: The function t is deferred entirely to the report.
literal_quantifiers: All integers d at least one and r at least two.
technical_assessment: Need the color-class sizes and partition condition before comparing colored Tverberg bounds; no alteration to standard formulations.

title: False Grassmannian bundle conjecture for symmetric powers
statement: Suppose $d$ and $k$ are even positive integers. Then there exists $n(d,k)$ such that, for every section of the bundle $\Sigma^d(\gamma_n^k)$ over $G_n^k$, with $n\ge n(d,k)$, there exists a subspace $V\in G_n^k$ such that this section is a multiple of $(Q(\gamma_n^k))^{d/2}$ over $V$.
completeness_reason: Grassmannian, bundle, Q and section regularity conventions are not supplied.
literal_quantifiers: Even positive d,k, eventually all n and all sections.
technical_assessment: Title says false but is not evidence. A characteristic-class obstruction would need exact real/oriented bundle and allowed sections; no certificate claimed.

title: Gromov–Milman conjecture for homogeneous polynomials
statement: For every even positive integer $d$ and every positive integer $k$, there exists an integer $n(d,k)$ such that, for every homogeneous polynomial $f$ of degree $d$ on $\fR^n$ with $n\ge n(d,k)$, there is a linear $k$-dimensional subspace $V\subseteq\u0007fR^n$ for which $f|_V$ is proportional to the $d/2$-th power of the standard quadratic form $Q=x_1^2+x_2^2+\cdots+x_n^2$.
completeness_reason: Real homogeneous polynomials and quadratic restriction condition specify the assertion despite recoverable encoding noise.
literal_quantifiers: Every even d and positive k; eventually every ambient dimension and every degree-d polynomial.
technical_assessment: Quadratic case follows from eigenvalue compression but supplies no all-degree theorem; higher-degree simultaneous restriction is not solved by that instance.

title: Lower bound for the second h-number of a simplicial cell decomposition of the 3-torus
statement: Prove that if $P$ is a simplicial cell decomposition of the 3-dimensional torus $T^3=S^1\times S^1\times S^1$, then $h_2(P)\ge 22$.
completeness_reason: Simplicial cell decomposition and h2 conventions require definition, especially multiple cells with same vertices.
literal_quantifiers: Every simplicial cell decomposition of the three-torus.
technical_assessment: A general lower-bound theorem for manifold simplicial posets is a plausible bridge; no theorem body checked, so not classified as known or new.

title: Quantization commutes with reduction for proper cocompact actions
statement:
Under the hypotheses of the Hochs–Landsman conjecture, there exists a positive integer $p_0$ such that, for every integer $p\ge p_0$,
\[
\left(\int_G\right)^*\!\circ\mu_M^G\bigl([\eth_M^{L^p}]\bigr)=\operatorname{index}\bigl(\eth_{M_G}^{L_G^p}\bigr).
\]
If $G$ has an $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant metric, one may take $p_0=1$.
completeness_reason: All Hochs-Landsman hypotheses, action data and several operators are omitted.
literal_quantifiers: Eventually all tensor powers p, with p0=1 under an invariant-metric condition.
technical_assessment: Index-theoretic comparison requires properness, cocompactness and reduction regularity recovered from source; no finite certificate route.

title: Positivity conjecture for refined Donaldson–Thomas invariants
statement: Assume that $Q$ is a symmetric quiver. For every stability parameter $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{Q_0}$ and every $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^{Q_0}$, the function $\Omega^\theta_\alpha(-q^{1/2})$ is a Laurent polynomial in $q^{1/2}$ with non-negative integer coefficients; equivalently, $\Omega^\theta_\alpha(-q^{1/2})\in\mathbb{N}[q^{\pm 1/2}]$.
completeness_reason: Refined DT invariant Omega and stability convention are undefined.
literal_quantifiers: Every symmetric quiver, real stability parameter and dimension vector.
technical_assessment: Positivity depends on normalization and cohomological realization; possible established positivity theorem remains only a prior lead without a body.

title: Generic basis conjecture beyond the Buan–Iyama–Reiten–Scott setting
statement:
The authors of [11] conjecture that the set
\[
\left\{x_e\psi_Z\ \middle|\ Z\text{ is strongly reduced},\ e\in\mathbb N^{Q_0},\ \operatorname{supp}(e)\cap\operatorname{supp}(\dim Z)=\varnothing\right\}
\]
is a basis of the associated cluster algebra \(A_Q\) even outside the setting of Example 2.
completeness_reason: Q, psi, strongly reduced and Example 2 are source-specific absent data.
literal_quantifiers: Every strongly reduced component and disjoint-support exponent in an unspecified associated cluster algebra.
technical_assessment: Generic-basis and specialization mechanisms cannot be assessed until the algebra and coefficient ring are fixed.

title: Indecomposable tree modules for every root
statement: Let $k=\\mathbb{C}$ and let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1)$ be a quiver without oriented cycles. Does there exist an indecomposable tree module for every root $d\in\mathbb{N}^{Q_0}$?
completeness_reason: Root and tree-module conventions are not defined in the literal.
literal_quantifiers: Every acyclic quiver over C and every root dimension vector.
technical_assessment: Exceptional real roots do not cover imaginary roots or parameter families; no constructive full-root mechanism supplied.

title: Computational interpretation of all the axioms
statement: The report conjectures that a computational interpretation of all the axioms is possible, defining equality on a type by recursion on that type, extending Gandy’s 1956 definition for simple type theory. For this interpretation, it expects the equality $\operatorname{Id}_{B(a)}(b\mathbin{\cdot}1_a)\,b$ to hold only as a propositional equality and not as a definitional equality.
completeness_reason: All the axioms and the intended computational interpretation are not specified.
literal_quantifiers: An interpretation of an omitted type theory, including a propositional equality requirement.
technical_assessment: No fixed syntax, reduction relation or soundness target; cannot test a universal interpretation literally.

title: Unique algorithm generating the 15 rows of Plimpton 322
statement: Are the 15 rows the result of a unique algorithm?
completeness_reason: The 15 rows and admissible algorithm class and equivalence are absent.
literal_quantifiers: Uniqueness of an unspecified historical generating algorithm.
technical_assessment: Infinitely many programs reproduce any finite table unless a model class is fixed; this is an underdetermination objection, not a new theorem.

title: Kernel generation for the longest intertwining operator
statement:
Let \(\pi=L_Q(\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_k)\) be an arbitrary irreducible representation, and let \(K=\ker M(w_0)\) be the kernel of the longest intertwining operator, equivalently the kernel of the projection \(\delta_1\times\cdots\times\delta_k\to\pi\). Is it true in general that
\[
K=\sum_{w=w_1w_2:\,w_1\text{ a simple reflection},\,M_{w_2}\text{ an isomorphism}}\ker M_w?
\]
completeness_reason: Representation group, induction conventions and intertwiner normalization are absent.
literal_quantifiers: Every irreducible LQ(delta1,...,deltak) in the unstated category.
technical_assessment: Rank-one kernels and braid decompositions need precise reducibility data; a formal Coxeter factorization does not establish the sum of kernels.

title: Wavelet-basis independence for leader scaling functions with finitely smooth wavelets
statement: For a bounded function $f$, does the leader scaling function $\[1m\eta_f(p)\u001b[0m$ remain independent of the choice of wavelet basis for every $p\in\mathbb{R}$ when the wavelets have only finite smoothness, for example when they are compactly supported?
completeness_reason: Leader scaling function and wavelet admissibility and smoothness thresholds are absent.
literal_quantifiers: Every bounded f and every real p, over finitely smooth wavelet bases.
technical_assessment: Negative moments and vanishing coefficients can change scaling; basis-change estimates require exact leader definition and regularity class.

title: Existence of a real rational plane quartic through 11 generic real points
statement: There exists a real rational plane quartic through 11 generic real points.
completeness_reason: Generic lacks real Zariski-open versus almost-everywhere and curve singularity conventions.
literal_quantifiers: Eleven generic real plane points; existence of a real rational quartic.
technical_assessment: Enumerative counts suggest an odd signed-count route, but using a public enumerative theorem would be an adaptation; no new mechanism claimed.

title: Centers of centralizer algebras for symmetric groups
statement: Let $S_l\leq S_n$ be the subgroup of permutations fixing every number larger than $l$, and write $\mathbb{Z}S_n^{S_l}=\{a\in\mathbb{Z}S_n:ah=ha\ \text{for all }h\in S_l\}$. Is $Z(\mathbb{Z}S_n^{S_l})$ generated, as a $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra, by $Z(\mathbb{Z}S_n)$ and $Z(\mathbb{Z}S_l)$?
completeness_reason: Integral centralizer algebra and generating subalgebras are explicitly given.
literal_quantifiers: Every symmetric group size n and subgroup Sl with l at most n.
technical_assessment: Rational semisimple centers do not imply integral generation; a lattice-index obstruction or integral basis argument is needed. No finite instance would prove all n,l.

title: Hill’s conjecture on invariant factors of Cartan matrices of Hecke-algebra blocks
statement: For \(\ell=p^r\), Hill computed the invariant factors of the Cartan matrix associated with an individual block of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra \(H_n\) when \(r\le p\), and conjectured that the same formula holds for arbitrary \(r\).
completeness_reason: The invariant-factor formula being asserted is absent.
literal_quantifiers: Prime-power ell=p^r for arbitrary r, all corresponding blocks.
technical_assessment: Cannot compute or falsify a formula not present; retain missing-scope row.

title: Existence of ordinary-character basic sets
statement: For every finite group $G$ and prime $p$, does there exist a basic set $BS$ contained in $\operatorname{Irr}(G)$? Equivalently, can one always choose ordinary irreducible characters whose restrictions to the $p$-regular elements form a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis for the Grothendieck group of Brauer characters?
completeness_reason: Equivalent character-restriction basis formulation specifies integral, not merely rational, spanning.
literal_quantifiers: Every finite group and prime p.
technical_assessment: A full-rank decomposition matrix need not contain a unimodular maximal minor; ordinary rational basis extraction does not settle the required Z-basis.

title: Foulkes’ Conjecture
statement: For $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $m<n$, let $H^{(m^n)}$ be the permutation module for $S_{mn}$ acting on set partitions of a set of size $mn$ into $n$ sets of size $m$, and let $\phi^{(m^n)}$ be its character. Foulkes conjectured that, for every irreducible character $\chi^\lambda$ of $S_{mn}$, $\langle \phi^{(m^n)},\chi^\lambda\rangle\geq \langle \phi^{(n^m)},\chi^\lambda\rangle$.
completeness_reason: Permutation action, multiplicities and m<n quantifiers are explicit.
literal_quantifiers: All positive m<n and all partitions lambda of mn.
technical_assessment: Induced-module dimension inequalities cannot prove each irreducible multiplicity inequality; no uniform injection established.

title: Thin-shell concentration conjecture of Anttila, Ball, and Perissinaki
statement: There exists a sequence $(\varepsilon_n)$ with $\varepsilon_n\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$ such that, for every isotropic log-concave random vector $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $$\mathbb{P}\left(\left||X|_2-\sqrt{n}\right|\geq\varepsilon_n\sqrt{n}\right)\leq\varepsilon_n.$$
completeness_reason: Probability inequality and uniform dimensional sequence are explicit.
literal_quantifiers: One epsilon sequence tending to zero, every isotropic log-concave vector in each dimension.
technical_assessment: This is relative shell concentration, weaker than constant shell width; a known concentration theorem may subsume it. No current primary body checked, so HOLD rather than novelty clearance.

title: Compressed-sensing recovery from a kernel-diameter condition
statement:
Let $0<r\le p<\infty$, let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times N}$, and let $1\le m\le N$. Writing $q$ so that $\frac1p+\frac1q=\frac1r$, if
\[
\operatorname{diam}_p\bigl(\ker A\cap B_N^r\bigr)<\frac{1}{2m^{1/q}},
\]
then $A$ satisfies the $\ell_r$-minimization problem for every $x\in\operatorname{sparse}(m)$; namely, $x$ is the unique solution of
\[
\min\{\lvert t\rvert_r^r:t\in\mathbb{R}^N,\ At=Ax\}.
\]
completeness_reason: Norm diameter, all parameter ranges, sparse vector and exact minimization are specified; q=infinity uses standard reciprocal convention.
literal_quantifiers: All 0<r<=p<infinity, matrices A and support bounds m.
technical_assessment: Primary report already labels the assertion Theorem 7; literal r>1 also has an exact convex-objective obstruction. Range correction/public theorem earns no credit. See bounded-checks and selected-passages.

title: Linear growth of an entry in a random contingency table
statement: Suppose that $m=n$ and $R=C=(3n,n,\ldots,n)$. Let $D$ be chosen uniformly at random from $A_+(R,C)$, the set of $n\times n$ matrices with non-negative integer entries and row sums $R$ and column sums $C$. Is it true that the expectation of the $(1,1)$ entry of $D$ grows linearly in $n$ as $n$ grows?
completeness_reason: Uniform distribution and all row and column margins are given.
literal_quantifiers: All n asymptotically; expected first entry has linear order of growth.
technical_assessment: Typical-table phase-transition estimates could give full asymptotics, but symmetry and margin totals alone do not give a linear lower bound. No short certificate route.

title: Universal diffusion exponent for the wind-tree model
statement: For every $(a,b)\in(0,1)^2$, for almost every direction $\theta$ and every point $x\in T(a,b)$ with an infinite trajectory, $$\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac{\log d\bigl(x,\phi_t^\theta(x)\bigr)}{\log t}=\frac{2}{3}.$$
completeness_reason: Wind-tree table T, flow and metric are not defined in the literal.
literal_quantifiers: Every obstacle parameter pair, almost every direction, every infinite-trajectory point.
technical_assessment: Almost every parameter results would not settle every parameter, and almost every starting point would not settle every point; no quantifier bridge asserted.

title: Pure periodicity versus torus branched coverings
statement: Does pure periodicity imply that a translation surface is a torus branched covering? Here, a translation surface is purely periodic if, for every direction $\theta\in S^1$, the existence of a nonsingular periodic orbit in direction $\theta$ implies that the directional flow $\varphi_\theta$ is periodic, i.e. there exists $t>0$ such that $\varphi_\theta^t=\operatorname{Id}$ almost everywhere.
completeness_reason: Compactness, singularities and area assumptions on translation surfaces are unstated.
literal_quantifiers: All translation surfaces satisfying the explicitly quantified pure-periodicity property.
technical_assessment: Commensurable cylinder periods are necessary locally, but deriving a global rank-two period lattice requires a real theorem, not isolated cylinder calculations.

title: Hilbert modular varieties and the Schottky locus
statement: Conjecture: For every sufficiently large genus $g$, all but finitely many Hilbert modular varieties in $\mathcal A_g$ are disjoint from the Schottky locus $t(\mathcal M_g)$.
completeness_reason: Hilbert modular varieties need level, irreducibility and counting-up-to-image conventions.
literal_quantifiers: Eventually every genus, finitely many exceptional varieties in each genus.
technical_assessment: Dimension heuristics cannot prove disjointness of every remaining special locus; no effective global intersection bound supplied.

title: Semisimplicity of the division closure for groups with bounded torsion
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a group whose finite subgroups have uniformly bounded orders, and let $D_\Gamma$ be the division closure of $\mathbb{Z}\Gamma$ in the algebra $U_\Gamma$ of affiliated operators. Is $D_\Gamma$ a semisimple Artinian ring, equivalently a direct sum of matrix rings over skew fields?
completeness_reason: Bounded torsion and division closure inside affiliated operators specify the ring question.
literal_quantifiers: Every group with uniformly bounded finite-subgroup orders.
technical_assessment: Torsion-free cases already require deep division-ring control; testing finite groups or standard classes cannot settle all groups.

title: Vanishing theorem for negative K-groups and K-regularity
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over a field $F$ of characteristic $0$, and suppose that the dimension of $X$ is $d$. Then $NK_i(X)=0$ for all $d\le -i$, and, in fact, $X$ is $K_{-d}$-regular. Moreover, $K_i(X)=0$ for $i<-d$, and $K_{-d}(X)$ can be computed explicitly in terms of a resolution of the singularities of $X$.
completeness_reason: Vanishing and regularity clauses are precise but computed explicitly supplies no endpoint formula.
literal_quantifiers: All finite-type schemes over characteristic-zero fields, degrees at and below negative dimension.
technical_assessment: Negative K-theory descent may already establish the named vanishing; explicit-resolution clause is unspecified and no full dependency body checked.

title: Hypothesis A on the Euler and Pontryagin classes of $B\mathrm{STOP}(2m)$
statement: Hypothesis A asserts that, for every positive integer $m$, $p_m=e^2\in H^{4m}(B\mathrm{STOP}(2m);\mathbb{Q})$, where $e$ is the Euler class and $p_m$ is the Pontryagin class.
completeness_reason: Rational cohomology classes, degree and universal oriented topological bundle space are specified.
literal_quantifiers: Every positive m, equality of top Pontryagin class and squared Euler class.
technical_assessment: Smooth-bundle identity does not transfer to B STOP without controlling the topological/smooth comparison fiber; no short bridge.

title: Hypothesis B on smooth maps to the plane
statement: For all even integers $n\ge 4$, the map $\nabla$ is rationally nullhomotopic with derived $O(2)$-invariance.
completeness_reason: Map nabla, source, target and derived invariance action are absent.
literal_quantifiers: All even n at least four.
technical_assessment: No nullhomotopy can be constructed for an undefined map; retain literal missing-scope classification.

title: Beilinson’s non-degeneracy conjecture for Chow groups
statement:
For all smooth and proper schemes $X$ over a finite field, the intersection pairing
$$CH^{n}(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}\times CH_{n}(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}\longrightarrow CH_{0}(X)\longrightarrow \mathbb{Q}$$
is non-degenerate.
completeness_reason: Rational Chow intersection and degree pairing specify nondegeneracy using standard conventions.
literal_quantifiers: Every smooth proper finite-field scheme and each admissible cycle degree n.
technical_assessment: Numerical versus rational equivalence is a deep global obstruction; finite examples cannot settle all schemes.

title: Uniqueness of the Brownian map
statement: Can different subsequential Gromov–Hausdorff limits of rescaled uniformly distributed rooted planar $q$-angulations, or different admissible values of $q$ (namely $q=3$ or even $q\ge 4$), yield different limiting metric spaces? Equivalently, is the metric on the quotient space $\mathbf m_\infty$ uniquely determined, independently of the subsequence and of $q$?
completeness_reason: Rescaling constants, random-limit equivalence and quotient metric construction are omitted.
literal_quantifiers: All admissible q and all subsequential scaling limits.
technical_assessment: Uniqueness-in-law and equality of coupled metrics are different; Brownian-map uniqueness is a plausible existing-result lead, not checked proof-body evidence.

title: Veech groups among finite-index subgroups of $SL_2(\d53d)$
statement: Is it true that every finite-index subgroup of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ is a Veech group?
completeness_reason: Veech group category does not specify compact finite-type versus general translation surfaces.
literal_quantifiers: Every finite-index subgroup of SL2(Z).
technical_assessment: Origami stabilizers and general translation-surface realization differ; finite-index group enumeration alone cannot provide the all-subgroup construction.

title: McCallum–Sharifi generation conjecture
statement:
For every odd prime $p$ and every integer $r\ge 1$, let $A_r=\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{p^r}))\{p\}$ and let $A_r^{-}$ be its minus part under complex conjugation. Then $A_r^{-}/p^rA_r^{-}$ is generated by the elements
\[
\{1-\zeta_{p^r}^{u},\,1-\zeta_{p^r}^{v}\},\qquad u,v\in\mathbb{Z}/p^r\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\},
\]
where the braces denote the stated cup-product pairing.
completeness_reason: Cup product, its cohomological domain and map into class-group quotient are omitted.
literal_quantifiers: Every odd prime p and r at least one, all displayed cyclotomic-unit pairs.
technical_assessment: Class-group computations for finitely many p,r are not a universal generation proof; pairing normalization and ramification must be recovered first.
